disclaimer: ADVISORY ONLY. Through-check policy varies by carrier, by airport, by whether the itinerary is interline, and by what is in the bag. Every row is a prompt to confirm at check-in, not an authority. Where a value is unknown the engine says so rather than assuming the traveller's bag will follow them.

the_24_hour_line_again.finding: The same 24-hour boundary that separates a stopover from a connection also governs baggage on most carriers. ANA states it directly: baggage is checked through only on a same-day connection, and under 24 hours it should reach the final destination. The general interline convention matches — beyond 24 hours on an international itinerary the break is a stopover, and the traveller collects and re-checks.
the_24_hour_line_again.why_that_is_good_news: The app's 8-24h overnight sweet spot sits UNDER the line on most carriers, so bags are normally through-checked. The traveller walks into the city with a daypack rather than a suitcase.
the_24_hour_line_again.the_trap: US carriers cap it far lower than 24 hours — American around 12 (raised to roughly 16.5 on American and American-to-partner itineraries) and United around 12. A 16-hour layover is comfortably inside ANA's limit and outside United's. That difference is invisible unless the app says so.
the_24_hour_line_again.second_trap: Korean customs require passengers arriving on an international flight to collect baggage at their first point of entry in Korea and clear customs, regardless of through-check status. An overnight in Seoul means handling the bag whatever the tag says.

NH.name: All Nippon Airways
NH.note: Baggage checked through only on a same-day connection; under 24h it should reach the final destination.

JL.name: Japan Airlines
JL.note: Through-checks to the destination, with exceptions for fragile items, sports equipment, instruments, pets and high-value baggage, which must be collected and re-checked. The 24h figure is the industry convention rather than a quoted JAL limit.

KE.name: Korean Air
KE.note: Reported working on a 13h ICN layover on a single reservation. See the Korean customs note — an overnight in Korea means collecting the bag regardless.

OZ.name: Asiana Airlines
OZ.note: Korean customs require collection at the first point of entry in Korea.

BR.name: EVA Air
BR.note: On a stopover, the baggage policy of the most significant operating carrier applies per sector.

CI.name: China Airlines
CI.note: Industry convention; not verified against China Airlines' own pages.

AA.name: American Airlines
AA.extended_note: Raised to roughly 16.5h on American and American-to-partner itineraries.
AA.note: WELL BELOW the 24h most non-US carriers allow. A 16h layover clears ANA's limit and fails American's base figure.

UA.name: United Airlines
UA.note: Around 12h — well below the 24h convention elsewhere.

DL.name: Delta Air Lines
DL.note: Reported to through-check generally on a single ticket, with no widely quoted hour limit. Treated as unknown rather than unlimited.
